liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Bob plays a faint China Cat Sunflower lick at 3:11 in the solo before the last verse; Scarlet to Fire is top five all time, with seamless transition and exhaustive tonal exploration [19][20]
- **Dancing In The Street** (1 review): Dancing In The Street closed the first set with high energy, described as a spinner's dream [13]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Second set is a long jam starting with Estimated Prophet, featuring amazing improvising [9]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): A rare and gorgeous Comes A Time, played only five times in 1977, closes the set [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-05-04.sbd.miller.91970.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 17 songs; 170 min; rated 4.42/5 by 26 [1]
- **gd1977-05-04.mtx.seamons.ht09.99106.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 17 songs; 175 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [2]
- **gd77-05-04.sbd.mccarthy.1321.sbefixed.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 156 min; rated 4.14/5 by 22 [4]. Said about its sound: The recording is described as flawless, with incredible sound quality throughout the second set; Under Garcia's solo, Weir's China Cat lick is audible; the jam is quiet and dreamy; Sound quality is poor until Brown Eyed Women; Fire is hot, and Playin' is long and spacy [10][11][14][15]
- **gd77-05-04.set1-sbd.minches.17967.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 10 songs; 94 min; rated 4.5/5 by 6 [5]
- **gd1977-05-04.151751.1st.set.shure.sm57.sublette.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 10 songs; 91 min [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-05-04.sbd.miller.91970.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Cassette -> ART DIO -> Cool Edit 2000 -> FLAC DSet 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD D [1]. Also: Set 1 SBD supplied by David Gans, transferred by David Minches from Sony ECM33P cassette master [1]
- **gd1977-05-04.mtx.seamons.ht09.99106.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [2]. Also: All transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller; Set 2 used SBD, Master Reel, Dat, and CD sources [2]
- **gd77-05-04.sbd.mccarthy.1321.sbefixed.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Set 1 has two extra generations; a newer SBDMC>C>CDR source is superior, though still worse than Set 2 [16]
- **gd77-05-04.set1-sbd.minches.17967.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Minches; source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Set 1 source has two additional generations; a newer SBDMC>C>CDR lineage is superior but inferior to Set 2 [17]
- **gd1977-05-04.151751.1st.set.shure.sm57.sublette.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Kathy Sublette; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Kathy Sublette's Master Audience Cassettes; Shure SM57 mics > Sony-TC158 [6]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks, Volume 50 (The Palladium, New York, NY - 5/3/77) 2024 US 4-CD set](https://us.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-50-the-palladium-new-york-ny-5-3-77-us-4-cd-album-set-r2726104-866521) [22]
- Poster by Pete Mason: [Dave’s Picks Volume 50 features Spring 1977 Grateful Dead](https://nysmusic.com/2023/12/17/daves-picks-volume-50-features-spring-1977-grateful-dead/) [23]
- Fan art by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful; Dead - Dave's Pick's #50 1977-04-04 The Palladium, New York City, NY](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2024/05/grateful-dead-daves-picks-50-1977-04-04.html) [24]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful; Dead - Dave's Pick's #50 1977-04-04 The Palladium, New York City, NY](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2024/05/grateful-dead-daves-picks-50-1977-04-04.html) [25]
- Poster by Worthpoint: [Grateful Dead DAVE'S PICKS 50 May 1977 Palladium NYC 5/3/77 3CD New #9230/25000 | #4914754871](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/grateful-dead-daves-picks-50-1977-4914754871) [26]
